chunks: Amali of al-Saduq: Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isam, from al-Kulayni, from 'Allan, from Muhammad ibn al-Faraj al-Rukhaji who said:

I wrote to Abi al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them) asking him about what Hisham ibn al-Hakam said regarding 'the body', and what Hisham ibn Salim said regarding 'the form'. He wrote (peace be upon him): Leave aside the confusion of the confused, and seek refuge in Allah from the Shaytan, the (true) position is not what was said by the two Hishams.

key_terms.الْهِشَامَانِ: The two Hishams (referring to Hisham ibn al-Hakam and Hisham ibn Salim)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali ibn Muhammad say about the views of Hisham ibn al-Hakam and Hisham ibn Salim on divine corporeality?
ai.summary: This hadith from Amali al-Saduq addresses the theological concept of divine corporeality (tajsim) by evaluating the nuanced positions of two prominent scholars, Hisham ibn al-Hakam and Hisham ibn Salim. The Imam's response rejects their specific formulations, advising the reader to avoid the confusion of those who over-analyze and to seek refuge from error, implying that the true understanding of God's attributes transcends simple physical categorization. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on distinguishing between God's essence and attributes without reducing them to material forms.
